text:
Joel Farabee arrived in Calgary as a scorer looking for a role. He found one early this season: 18 points in 24 games, 9 on the power play, and 66 shots, at more than 19 minutes a night. Last season he had 38 points in 82.

The last ten games have cooled things off. Three points where our numbers expected about 8.0. It's some of each: Calgary is getting fewer chances with him on the ice (9.3 expected goals against 11.2 usual), and his finishing has slipped. His ice time is up 1:48 a night anyway, so the coaches haven't lost faith.

The bigger picture is encouraging. He's creating 1.14 expected goals per 60 on his own, a large jump from 0.71 last season, so the shot quality is real. He has 7 goals on 8.8 expected, which means if anything he's owed a couple. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 61% of his shots coming off the rush last season, a transition-heavy game. Our middle projection is 25 goals.
headline: Farabee's chances are up, his points are not
